summary: preinstall drops Bun runtime to execute an obfuscated bundle unrelated to package purpose
details: The package declares a preinstall hook (`node setup.mjs`) that downloads a per-platform Bun runtime binary from GitHub releases, extracts it to a temp directory, chmods it executable, and immediately invokes it against `math_init.js` — a 727 KB single-line bundle with a string-array rotator (`WV8StW`), hex-mangled identifiers, and a `// @bun @bun-cjs` header that makes it runnable only under Bun. The stated purpose of the package is an OAuth token-refresh helper (`index.js`); `math_init.js` is not referenced from that entry point and its content is not documented. Additional impersonation signals include a dependency on `loadsh` (a known typosquat of `lodash`) and a README that names the package `authorizer-2-handler` while the published name is `@onereach/authorizer-helper`. Fetching a second language runtime specifically to execute an in-tree obfuscated bundle at install time is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern: attacker-controlled code executes on `npm install` outside of Node's normal inspection paths.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
